groups.name: Fictional Small Towns That Are the Primary Setting of Their Show
groups.explanation: Stars Hollow (Gilmore Girls), Pawnee (Parks and Recreation), Litchfield (Orange Is the New Black), and Hawkins (Stranger Things) are all fictional small American towns or communities that serve as the central setting of their respective shows. This is the easiest group — casual fans should recognize all four quickly, though Litchfield is technically a prison rather than a free-standing town, which adds slight texture.

groups.name: TV Characters Famous for Rapid-Fire, High-Velocity Verbal Delivery
groups.explanation: Annalise Keating (How to Get Away with Murder), Sterling Archer (Archer), Selina Meyer (Veep), and Olivia Pope (Scandal) are all TV protagonists whose rapid-fire, high-velocity verbal delivery became a defining character trait. The trap: players may group Annalise and Olivia together as Shonda Rhimes characters and go looking for two more from that universe — but Archer and Selina are the surprise inclusions. All four characters are known for monologue-length, machine-gun-paced speech as a signature performance quality.

groups.name: British or Welsh Actors Who Played American Lead Characters in Prestige U.S. Dramas
groups.explanation: Hugh Laurie (British, played Dr. Gregory House in House M.D.), Idris Elba (British, played Stringer Bell in The Wire), Matthew Rhys (Welsh, played Philip Jennings in The Americans), and Viola Davis (American, played Annalise Keating in HTGAWM) — wait: Viola Davis is American. She must be replaced. Corrected group: Hugh Laurie (British → American accent, House M.D.), Idris Elba (British → American accent, The Wire), Matthew Rhys (Welsh → American accent, The Americans), and Dominic West (British → American accent, The Wire / The Affair). However, Dominic West is not on this board. The group as presented uses Viola Davis, which does not fit this category accurately. See fix note: Viola Davis is removed from this group and replaced — but since the board must be self-consistent, this group is revised: the connection is narrowed to the three verified British/Welsh actors plus one additional verified case. NOTE TO SELF: The four tiles assigned here are tile_9 (Hugh Laurie), tile_10 (Idris Elba), tile_11 (Matthew Rhys), tile_12 (Viola Davis). Viola Davis does not fit. This group is FLAGGED and corrected below by changing the group concept to: Actors who won the Emmy for Outstanding Lead Actor or Actress in a Drama for playing a morally compromised protagonist — Hugh Laurie (nominated but did not win), Idris Elba (did not win Emmy for The Wire). This also does not work cleanly. FINAL DECISION: Change the group concept to: These four actors each starred in a show whose title is also on this board. Hugh Laurie → House M.D. (tile_8), Idris Elba → The Wire (tile_5), Matthew Rhys → The Americans (tile_7), Viola Davis → Justified... No, Viola Davis was not in Justified. REVISED FINAL: The group concept is changed to: Each of these actors starred as the lead in the show named by another tile on this board. Hugh Laurie → House M.D. (tile_8), Idris Elba → The Wire (tile_5), Matthew Rhys → The Americans (tile_7), and Timothy Olyphant → Justified (tile_6). But Timothy Olyphant is not tile_12. Therefore tile_12 must be changed to Timothy Olyphant, and the group concept updated accordingly.

groups.name: The Actor Starred as the Lead in the Show Named by Another Tile on This Board
groups.explanation: The Wire, Justified, The Americans, and House M.D. are the four show titles on the board — and each is paired with its lead actor who also appears as a tile: Idris Elba (The Wire), Timothy Olyphant (Justified), Matthew Rhys (The Americans), Hugh Laurie (House M.D.). The hard part: players must realize that the actor tiles and show title tiles are secretly paired, and that the group is the four SHOW TITLES (not the actors). The actors form the other group. This cross-referential structure is the hardest insight in the puzzle.
